title: Modi Leaves for Europe Tomorrow With the Longest Agenda an Indian PM Has Carried to a G7.
excerpt: Five days, two countries, one historic first and a fraught bilateral with Trump. From dead Indian sailors to H-1B visas to a trade deal deadline, here is everything on the table.
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi departs on Friday for the most consequential foreign trip of his year — a five-day, two-country European tour that includes the first-ever visit by an Indian prime minister to Slovakia and a high-stakes bilateral meeting with Donald Trump at the G7 summit in Évian-les-Bains, France.

The trip begins in Nice on June 13, moves to Bratislava on June 14, returns to Évian for the G7 on June 16–17, and wraps in Paris on June 18 at VivaTech, Europe's largest startup and technology conference. It is Modi's seventh consecutive G7 appearance and India's 13th participation in the forum overall.

No Indian PM has walked into a G7 carrying a list this long. The agenda touches trade, visas, dead sailors, defence deals, artificial intelligence and India's place in a reordering global economy.

## Nice: Macron and the Innovation Play

Modi's first stop is a bilateral with French President Emmanuel Macron in Nice on June 14. The two leaders will review the India-France Special Global Strategic Partnership, upgraded earlier this year, with discussions expected to cover defence cooperation under "Make in India," joint ventures in nuclear energy and submarine manufacturing, and counter-terrorism coordination.

They will also jointly inaugurate "Bharat Innovates," a flagship event during the India-France Year of Innovation that brings together startups and venture capital from both countries. France has emerged as India's closest European partner on defence and technology, and Macron has been lobbying to bring Indian semiconductor and AI investment to French industrial zones.

## Bratislava: A First in 33 Years

From Nice, Modi will fly to Slovakia for a state visit — the first by any Indian prime minister since the country's independence in 1993. The visit follows President Droupadi Murmu's trip to Bratislava in April 2025 and Slovak President Peter Pellegrini's attendance at India's AI Impact Summit in February.

Modi will hold talks with Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico, with discussions expected to cover trade, investment, and cooperation in automobile and railway manufacturing. Slovakia's automotive industry, which produces more cars per capita than any other country, aligns with India's push to localise EV and component supply chains.

## Évian: The Main Event

The G7 summit on June 16–17 in Évian-les-Bains — hosted by Macron and chaired by France — is where the highest-stakes conversations will happen.

The summit's formal agenda covers three sessions: forging new global partnerships, reviving balanced economic growth, and ensuring the safe rollout of artificial intelligence. India, Brazil, Kenya, South Korea and Syria have been invited as partner nations alongside the seven core members.

But the real action will happen on the margins. Modi is expected to hold a bilateral with Trump, and Indian government sources say three issues will dominate: trade, visas and energy cooperation.

**Trade:** Negotiations on a first-tranche India-US bilateral trade agreement are moving toward a mid-July deadline, according to Trade Minister Piyush Goyal. India is seeking preferential tariff treatment. Washington has countered with a proposed 12.5 per cent surcharge on Indian imports under a forced-labour allegation that India has firmly rejected, alongside a Section 301 investigation into Indian "overcapacity" in textiles and steel.

**Visas:** The H-1B programme remains a flashpoint. A federal judge this week blocked Trump's proposed $100,000 H-1B fee — a ruling that disproportionately benefits Indians, who hold 75 per cent of all approvals. But the administration's broader push to tighten immigration pathways remains intact, and Modi is expected to press for stability in visa processing.

**Seafarers and the Gulf:** The most emotionally charged item on the agenda arrived uninvited. Three Indian sailors were killed this week in US strikes on a tanker off Oman. India summoned the American envoy — twice in three days — and put all maritime agencies on heightened alert. Opposition parties have demanded Modi raise the issue directly with Trump. Doing so at the G7 bilateral would be diplomatically delicate but domestically necessary.

## Paris: VivaTech and the AI Pitch

Modi's final stop is VivaTech in Paris on June 18, where he will make India's case as an AI deployment market. With TCS signing up 50,000 employees for Anthropic's Claude, Infosys already partnered with the same company, and EY, Deloitte and SatSure all opening AI centres in Bengaluru this week, India's pitch at VivaTech will be backed by fresh announcements.

The trip is India's most ambitious multilateral engagement since the pandemic-era virtual summits gave way to in-person diplomacy. What Modi brings back — on tariffs, on visa policy, on energy assurances — will matter far beyond the communiqué.
